title: Testing Before You Trust
note: Testing ministers and others by their birth, character, understanding and deeds, then trusting them. A ruler marching on his enemy needs this so that work gets done and no one betrays him.

couplets.plain: Test someone by these four, righteousness, wealth, pleasure and fear for their life, and then trust them.
couplets.pm: A ruler should trust a man only after four trials of his mind, each put to him under oath. Priests say the ruler is unrighteous and must go. The general says he is a miser and must go. An old ascetic woman says a palace lady wants him. A minister says the ruler plans their deaths. If he never wavers, he never will. He rejects the variant உயிரெச்சம்.

links.reason: Three of its four tests are the aims of life: righteousness, wealth and pleasure.

couplets.plain: Trust the one who is born of good family, free of faults, and has the shame that dreads a scar.
couplets.pm: A ruler’s trust belongs with the man born of a high family, free of faults, who has the shame that fears a stain. The faults are the six named for rulers, with sloth, forgetfulness and error. Shame means a mind that won’t turn to low acts. These are learned mostly by hearing from worthy people. Trust only one who has all four.

links.quote: Trust the one who is born of good family
the shame that dreads a scar

couplets.plain: Even among those who have learned hard things and have no flaw, look closely and you will rarely find anyone with no ignorance at all.
couplets.pm: Even in those who have studied hard books and are free of the faults named, it is rare, if you examine closely, to find no ignorance. It shows in them only now and then, through the mind’s unsteadiness. The hint is that only those shown by direct observation to be free even of that should be trusted.

couplets.plain: Look at their good points, look at their faults, see which are more, and judge them by that.
couplets.pm: No one in the world has only virtues or only faults. So examine someone’s virtues, then their faults, find which side is greater, and know them by it. Greater means greater in importance or in number. If the virtues are greater they are fit for the work, and if the faults are, they are not. Since those with only virtues are rare, this is how to trust anyone.

links.quote: see which are more, and judge them by that

couplets.plain: For a person’s greatness or smallness, their own deeds are the touchstone.
couplets.pm: The touchstone for the greatness people reach by birth, character and understanding, and for their smallness, is the deeds they do, and nothing else. There are other ways of knowing, but deeds are the final one.

links.quote: their own deeds are the touchstone

couplets.plain: Do not trust those who have no one. They have no ties and feel no shame at blame.
couplets.pm: Don’t trust those with no kin. They have no bond with the world, so they don’t fear blame. People avoid what the world blames and do what it praises through the ways of life among kin, and those with no kin lack this. So they can’t be trusted.
couplets.sensitive: treats people without family as untrustworthy

links.quote: Do not trust those who have no one

couplets.plain: To trust those who don’t know what they should, leaning on your fondness for them, brings every kind of folly.
couplets.pm: To trust those who don’t know what they need to know, with loving-kindness as your prop, gives a ruler every kind of ignorance. If he hands work to the unwise out of the loving-kindness between them, it fails through their ignorance. Then the ignorance isn’t only theirs. He too is shown not to know whom to appoint or what would follow.

links.quote: leaning on your fondness for them
links.reason: Trusting on fondness in place of a proper trial brings every kind of folly.

couplets.plain: Trust a stranger without testing them, and the suffering won’t end, even for those who come after you.
couplets.pm: A ruler who trusts a man with no tie to him, without testing him by birth and deeds, gets suffering that lasts even into his line. The tie is a lineage joined to his own family, and this is needed too. Trusting means handing him the work. When it fails, those born of his family fall into enemy hands and are brought low.

links.quote: even for those who come after you
Trust a stranger without testing them

couplets.plain: Trust no one without testing them. After testing, trust them with what they can be trusted with.
couplets.pm: Don’t trust anyone without examining them, in any task. After examining, have no doubt about them in the tasks fit to give them. “Trust” here means setting doubt aside. What can be trusted means the work that suits each one’s ability.

links.quote: Trust no one without testing them

couplets.plain: To trust without testing, and to doubt someone you have come to trust, both bring suffering that doesn’t end.
couplets.pm: For a ruler to trust someone untested, and to doubt someone he has tested and trusted, both bring him lasting suffering. If he doubts a man after giving him work, with no fault seen, the man notices, decides the post won’t last and lets the work slide. Enemies can also easily turn him away. So doubt is wrong as well.

links.quote: to doubt someone you have come to trust
